items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: Indian equity benchmarks experienced a third consecutive session of declines due to selling pressure. Global cues remained weak, impacting market sentiment and performance. A recovery is possible if the index reclaims 22,800, while immediate support is at 22,600. Foreign institutional investors were net buyers, but the rupee fell against the dollar amid rising crude oil prices. Investors are advised to assess levels carefully as market volatility persists.

items.title: Government plans to pare stakes in 4 PSU banks to 75%
items.description: The Union government announced in the 2021-22 budget that, besides IDBI Bank, it would take up two public sector banks and one general insurance company for privatisation.

items.title: Stocks in news: Swiggy, Infosys, HPCL, eMudhra, Adani Power, Shriram Finance, Tata Motors and NLC India
items.description: Indian equity markets faced continued downward pressure, marked by persistent selling and negative global indicators. The Nifty 50 index saw a decline, with analysts pointing out critical resistance and support points. Numerous companies disclosed their financial results, showcasing a mix of profits and setbacks for the September quarter. As various firms prepare to announce their quarterly earnings, market participants should remain vigilant over the coming days.

items.title: Financials, FMCG lead FPI sell-off; IT stocks buck the trend in first half of October
items.description: In the early days of October, there was a notable retreat of foreign portfolio investors from several sectors, particularly in financial services and FMCG, which saw outflows of ₹8,634 crore and ₹8,172 crore respectively. Conversely, IT stocks caught a breath of investment, attracting ₹2,599 crore as they turned a new page in investor sentiment.

items.title: Stock Radar: HAL stock breaks out from a descending channel; time to buy?
items.description: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited has recently broken out from a descending channel, signaling upward price movement. Experts recommend buying the stock for a target of Rs 5,800 within the next four to six months. The stock has regained momentum after a period of consolidation and has reclaimed important moving averages. Both EMA and MACD indicators confirm the bullish trend observed in recent price action.

items.title: SBI weighs data leak impact, alerts cyber cover provider
items.description: SBI may seek a claim under a Rs 1,425-crore cyber insurance policy with Oriental Insurance following a suspected leak of customer data, people familiar with the matter told ET. "SBI is in the process of notifying the insurer about the claim," said a person aware of the development.

items.title: RBI asks banks, payment firms to forensically clear tech environments in case of a data breach
items.description: The RBI has asked financial entities to remove management and administrative interfaces from public internet access, enforce multi-factor authentication for administrative access, and restrict access to cloud and backend systems on a least-privilege basis. The measures include auditing source code, repositories, configuration files, client applications and cloud storage for exposed credentials, and immediately rotating and purging compromised credentials.

items.title: Sensex sinks over 1,000 pts from day's high, Nifty below 22,500. What's ahead for D-Street?
items.description: As oil prices soar, the Indian stock market has deepened its losses, with both Sensex and Nifty experiencing significant downturns. Broader markets have also retreated further into the negative. Nevertheless, analysts maintain that there are glimmers of hope for the upcoming week; a rally among large-cap stocks could pave the way for investor opportunities.

items.title: eMudhra shares crash another 4%, down 40% in 3 sessions. What's behind this free fall?
items.description: eMudhra will exit its global SSL/TLS certificate business following a security incident involving compromised private keys linked to eight intermediate Certificate Authority certificates. The segment contributes about 1% of its global revenue. The development follows a sharp 37% decline in eMudhra shares over the previous two trading sessions.

items.title: Nomura, Axis initiate coverage on 8 stocks with up to 30% upside potential. See full list
items.description: A host of domestic and global brokerages have initiated coverage on select Indian stocks across sectors such as aluminum, energy and internet. Analysts are bullish on major names such as Paytm, Vedanta Aluminum among others and forecast strong upside from current market levels. Here is a list of stocks on which brokerages initiated coverage.

items.title: Ola Electric shares dip 5% after Goldman Sachs downgrades stock to Sell. Here’s why
items.description: Ola Electric shares fell sharply on Friday after Goldman Sachs downgraded the stock to Sell from Neutral and cut its target price to Rs 23, implying a 28% downside. The brokerage lowered its FY27-FY29 revenue estimates by up to 10%, citing prolonged operating losses and challenges in sustaining market share.

items.title: Infosys shares jump 3% ahead of Q2 earnings announcement. What to expect?
items.description: Infosys shares rose on Friday ahead of the IT major’s Q2 FY27 results, with analysts expecting an 11% year-on-year rise in revenue and an 8% increase in net profit. Investors will track management commentary on client spending, large deal wins and AI-led pricing pressure, alongside the company’s full-year revenue growth guidance.

items.title: Swiggy shares crash 14%, hit 52-week low after Q2 results. Here’s why Jefferies, Nomura, Bernstein cut target price
items.description: Swiggy experienced a notable decline in share prices after announcing a Rs 922 crore loss for the quarter. Revenue from operations rose 36% year-on-year to Rs 7,571 crore, indicating some growth potential. However, the company's adjusted EBITDA loss widened, raising concerns among investors regarding its financial health. Analysts have revised target prices downward, citing challenges in the quick commerce segment.

items.title: Shellz India SME shares to list today; GMP indicates 4% potential gain
items.description: Shellz India is set to list on the BSE SME platform on October 23, with a grey market premium of around 4%, indicating a potential listing gain of 4%. Its IPO was subscribed 58.54 times overall, led by NIIs at 86.41 times, followed by retail investors at 56.09 times and QIBs at 41.92 times.

items.title: Stellar Start! Tonbo Imaging shares list at 66% premium over IPO price
items.description: Tonbo Imaging India made a noteworthy debut on the stock market with shares opening significantly above the IPO price. The company successfully raised Rs 852.18 crore through its public offering, consisting entirely of an offer for sale. Subscription rates for the IPO reached impressive levels, with retail and institutional investors showing strong interest. Financial performance indicated a decline in total income and profit after tax for the company.

items.title: South Korea's Kospi crashes 40% from June peak as AI frenzy fizzles out. Can this benefit Dalal Street?
items.description: South Korea's stock market hit all-time highs before a sharp decline, marked by a 40% drop in the Kospi index since June, which has significantly affected investor wealth. As South Korean investors grapple with this downturn, experts believe that India’s market might benefit, citing its diverse sectors. It's encouraged that investors proceed with caution, keeping an eye on local demand and foreign investments.

items.title: HPCL shares in focus as Q1 net profit slips 6% YoY, revenue rises 26%. Should you buy?
items.description: HPCL reported Q2 FY27 consolidated profit of Rs 3,625 crore, down 6% year-on-year, while revenue increased 26% to Rs 1.39 lakh crore. Gross refining margins improved significantly to $32.15 per barrel. Despite strong operational performance, shares remain under pressure in 2026. Motilal Oswal maintained a Buy recommendation on the stock.

items.title: Clean Science and Technology among 3 stocks rose above VWAP
items.description: On October 22, the closing prices of three stocks in the Nifty500 pack were more than 1.5% above their respective VWAPs (Volume Weighted Average Price), according to StockEdge’s technical scan data.When the closing price is above the VWAP, it means the stock closed at a price higher than its volume-weighted average traded price during the day. The VWAP gives greater weight to prices at which higher trading volumes occurred.

items.title: Swiggy among 4 F&O stocks with sharp rise in futures open interest
items.description: As of October 22, four stocks in the NSE F&O segment recorded a rise of more than 9% in futures open interest compared with the previous trading session, according to StockEdge’s F&O scan data.A rise in futures open interest indicates an increase in the number of active, unexpired futures contracts in a security. This may reflect market participants opening new positions or adding to existing ones.

items.title: Kaynes Technology among 3 stocks showing White Marubozu pattern
items.description: On October 22, three stocks in the Nifty 500 pack featured in StockEdge’s White Marubozu bullish scanner, according to its technical scan data.A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern in which the opening price is the lowest and the closing price is the highest during a given period. It is represented by a long white (or green) candlestick with no upper shadow and little or no lower shadow, reflecting strong upward price momentum during the session.

items.title: Tata Teleservices among 4 stocks showing RSI trending up
items.description: On October 22, four stocks in the Nifty 500 pack that gained over 3% were highlighted in the RSI Trending Up scan, based on data from StockEdge.An RSI Trending Up signal occurs when the Relative Strength Index (RSI) crosses above 50 from below, indicating strengthening momentum. RSI is a technical indicator commonly used by traders to assess price momentum and trend strength.

items.title: Zetwerk Manufacturing shares list at 5% premium over IPO price
items.description: The Rs 5,012.33 crore IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 2,830 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 14.45 crore shares worth approximately Rs 2,182 crore. While the proceeds from the fresh issue will go to the company, the OFS proceeds will accrue to the selling shareholders.

items.title: Bonfiglioli Transmissions shares to list today: Check GMP ahead of debut
items.description: The Rs 2,533.66 crore IPO comprised an offer for sale (OFS) of 4.32 crore shares, with no fresh issue component. As the offering was entirely an OFS, the company will not receive any proceeds from the IPO. Instead, the proceeds will go to the existing shareholders selling their stakes.

items.title: From mercury to gold? This San Francisco startup claims it can produce yellow metal at will
items.description: San Francisco-based startup Marathon Fusion claims to have converted mercury into stable gold using fusion-generated neutrons, at a rate 10 times the record set by CERN in 2025. However, it has not disclosed the quantity of gold produced, leaving the commercial potential of the breakthrough unclear.

items.title: D-Street bleeds! Market value of all BSE-listed firms falls below Rs 450 lakh crore for first time since April. More pain ahead?
items.description: The market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies fell below Rs 450 lakh crore for the first time since April as Sensex and Nifty extended losses for a fourth straight session. Nearly Rs 25 lakh crore has been wiped out this week, with soaring crude prices and rising bond yields weighing on sentiment.

items.title: These large-, mid- and small-cap stocks can give more than 20% return in 1 year, according to analysts
items.description: There is really no doubt about what will happen in the short term. It is going to be tough. Trying to guess the exact day when things will improve is a waste of effort. But a frightened market is exactly when it helps to look the other way. Because markets go too far in both directions, not only the one that is hurting today.

items.title: This Tata Group stock plunged 10% a day after rallying 19% post Q2 results. Do you own?
items.description: Tata Teleservices (Maharashtra) shares plunged on Friday, giving up some gains after rallying 19% in the previous session following its Q2 results. The stock fell to Rs 34.24 on the NSE. The company reported a net loss of Rs 59 crore in Q2 FY27, narrowing from Rs 321 crore a year earlier and Rs 72 crore in the previous quarter. Despite the improvement, the stock has declined over 30% in 2026 so far and 59% in three years.

items.title: Broader markets crash! Small, midcap indices tumble up to 4%. Why analysts are sounding the alarm
items.description: Smallcap and midcap stocks plunged up to 4% on Friday, extending a sharp weekly selloff as analysts warned that valuations remain difficult to justify. The Nifty Smallcap 250 index has fallen around 8% this week, while the Nifty Midcap 100 is down 6%, despite a resilient earnings growth outlook.

items.title: Cyient shares rally 9% after Q2 revenue rises 25%; board declares Rs 12/sh interim dividend
items.description: Cyient shares surged on Friday after the company reported a 25% year-on-year rise in consolidated revenue to Rs 2,235 crore in Q2 FY27. Net profit declined 8% to Rs 132 crore. The board declared an interim dividend of Rs 12 per share, while its DET business reported stronger revenue and order intake.

items.title: Nippon Silver ETF, other silver ETFs slide up to 4% as silver prices tumble. Here’s why
items.description: Silver ETFs tumble up to 4% as India permits 6,500 metric tonnes of silver imports over six months, raising expectations of easing domestic supply tightness and premiums. Higher interest rates, bond yields and a firm dollar add to pressure on bullion prices.

items.title: Christopher Wood swapped Nvidia for a Greek infrastructure stock. The bet is paying off
items.description: Jefferies’ Christopher Wood replaced Nvidia with Greek infrastructure company GEK TERNA in his global long-only equity portfolio in October 2025. Since then, GEK TERNA has gained 65% in US-dollar terms, compared with Nvidia’s 15%. The shift reflects Wood’s preference for infrastructure, fiscal reform and improving economic fundamentals over crowded AI trades.

items.title: Rs 9,000 crore wiped out in a day: Why Swiggy investors are losing patience with Instamart
items.description: Swiggy shares plunged on Friday, wiping out around ₹9,000 crore in market value as widening Instamart losses overshadowed food delivery growth. Following Q2 results, brokerages cut their price targets, citing deteriorating quick-commerce profitability. Instamart’s adjusted EBITDA loss widened to ₹895 crore from ₹778 crore, while its contribution margin deteriorated to -1.4% despite 13.4% sequential growth in net order value.

items.title: Sensex plunges 1,200 pts from day's high, Nifty below 22,400. 4 factors behind Rs 10 lakh crore wipeout
items.description: The Sensex and Nifty extended losses on Friday as crude oil prices surged and foreign investor selling resumed. The selloff wiped out nearly Rs 10 lakh crore in market value, with smallcap and midcap stocks leading declines. Oil supply concerns and geopolitical tensions weighed on investor sentiment.

items.title: Hindustan Zinc shares drop 4% as India allows large silver imports despite weak demand
items.description: Hindustan Zinc shares fell sharply on Friday after India issued permits to import 6,500 metric tonnes of silver over the next six months to meet festive-season demand. The move could ease domestic premiums amid weak demand, while silver futures declined around 3%. The stock is down over 18% so far in 2026.

items.title: Bharat Electronics among 4 Sensex stocks to hit 52-week lows; shares fall up to 9% in a month
items.description: On Friday, the benchmark Sensex fell 125 points to close at 73,123. Amid the market decline, four Sensex stocks touched fresh 52-week lows, marking their lowest price levels in the past year. A 52-week low represents the lowest price at which a stock has traded over the preceding 12 months and provides an indicator of its recent price performance.

items.title: Only 15% of midcap stocks above 50-DMA: Is buying the dip getting riskier? JM Financial spots signs of leadership shift
items.description: JM Financial warns midcap and smallcap leadership may weaken as market breadth deteriorates sharply. Largecaps show early recovery signals, but investors should remain cautious. Nifty holding 22,000 could trigger a rebound; breaking below risks a fall towards 20,500.

items.title: Market wrap: Eternal, Apollo Hospital, Shriram Finance, Adani Enterprises among top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Friday
items.description: Indian equity markets fell for a fourth consecutive session, with the Nifty 50 closing at 22,600 and Sensex at 73,123.83. Small-cap, mid-cap and metal stocks slumped as bearish technical signals heightened concerns about further selling pressure.

items.title: 5 stocks with consistent score improvement and upside potential of up to 29% in 1 year, according to analysts
items.description: Do not paint the whole market with one brush. Even in an extended fall like the current one, some parts of the economy still manage to hold up. And the surprise tends to come from the corner nobody was watching.

items.title: RBI governor reiterates listing requirement for top NBFCs as focus intensifies on Tata Sons
items.description: India's central bank governor said on Friday non-bank finance companies classified in the upper layer are required to list on the stock market, reiterating the Reserve Bank of India's stance on the listing of Tata Sons without commenting directly on the company.
